commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Curse of the Dead Gods is a third-person action dungeon crawler with an Indiana Jones-style hero, multiple weapons and abilities, and a core mechanic built around curses. Nearly every action (opening doors, buying, upgrading) can curse you, bringing big upsides and downsides that force you to adapt each run. He loves the crisp, meaningful combat and VFX, and finds it a very challenging but rewarding risk-reward game. He is surprised it did not get more recognition and places it in a solid A tier.
praise: Curse system that attaches big upsides and downsides to almost every action and reshapes each run
Amazing, crisp combat where every action feels meaningful, e.g. swinging a heavy hammer
Phenomenal visual effects and great overall visuals
Great boss fights and very unique enemy designs
criticism: Stamina must always be managed carefully, making it tough
Takes a long time to finish (about 20 hours for his one completion) with a lot of upgrading
unique_points: Curses as the defining mechanic, tied to nearly every interaction, with heavy upside/downside tradeoffs
Runs must be adjusted around the curse concept, which the devs put heavy focus on

design_criteria: Risk vs reward: curses give major upsides and downsides
Combat feel: crisp, meaningful weapon impact
Visual effects and visuals: phenomenal VFX and great look
Difficulty: very challenging, unforgiving parry, stamina pressure
Run/game length: about 20 hours to complete

community.one_liner: An isometric, Hades-adjacent action roguelite from Passtech Games where a treasure hunter delves procedurally generated Mesoamerican-themed temples, using parry-and-dodge combat, torch light management and a corruption/curse system.
community.consensus_summary: Generally well received: Steam sits at Very Positive (about 83% of roughly 9,200 reviews), critics land in the high 70s to low 80s, and the combat is the near-universal highlight. The dissent is about structure rather than feel: a repetitive, grindy loop, limited enemy/room/weapon variety, slow meta-progression, and a punishing, RNG-heavy final temple. It spent about a year in Early Access (from March 2020) and launched fully on 23 Feb 2021 on PC, Switch, PS4 and Xbox One; post-launch support included a Dead Cells crossover in April 2021. Players often describe it as Hades on hard mode, but with much less story and personality, and it tends to be recommended to people who already like skill-based action more than to genre newcomers.
best_things: Crunchy, responsive combat built on parry, perfect dodge and weapon combos; many reviewers (critic and player) rate it above Hades for feel and fairness
Skill-first design: limited randomness in weapons and synergies means learning enemies and patterns, not build luck, decides runs
Light and darkness system: braziers and the torch reveal traps and reduce danger, and fire can turn enemies into light sources, adding a tactical layer
Curse/corruption mechanic creates risk-reward decisions (taking curses or trading blood for loot) and runs with real tension
Bosses with thematic, readable patterns, each tied to a god's domain (power, knowledge, etc.)
Strong atmosphere and art direction for the Aztec/Maya-inspired temples, with good sound design (for example the death-whistle perfect-dodge cue)
Large weapon roster (claws, swords, hammers, etc.) with different movesets, plus pleasant pick-up-and-put-down run length
Polished after a long Early Access period; performs well and is playable on controller and Switch
worst_things: Repetition: the same limited set of rooms, traps, enemies and bosses are learned by heart within roughly 15 hours, and the structure forces replaying earlier temples to reach later ones
Story and characters are thin to non-existent, so there is little narrative pull to keep running
Late-game difficulty feels cheap to many: teleporting, briefly invulnerable enemies, area attacks and health-sponge elites in the last temples
Final temple is long and grindy, with heavy gold requirements for final sacrifices and a DPS-check final boss that players call a wall
Weapon balance is uneven; some players feel fast weapons like claws dominate and other weapons are technically viable but worse
Curses often feel weak or randomly punishing: some reviewers say they rarely affect a run, while in the last temple the health-draining curse can leave you one hit from death
Slow, low-value meta-progression: unlocks cost a lot of crystal skulls for marginal gains
Achievements (including memoir-style completionist ones) are seen as grindy for 100% runs
Heavy reliance on RNG (starting items, late-game luck) makes the back half feel slow and unfair, and several reviewers say the final boss is a chore rather than a challenge
improvements: More enemy, room, boss and weapon variety so later runs feel different
Faster or more meaningful meta-progression, and fewer repeat traversals of earlier temples
Better tuning of the final temple: less elite health-sponge padding, more viable dexterity/damage builds, and a fairer gold requirement
More story, characters or lore payoff to give a reason to keep running
More reliable tools for managing corruption, so the curse system feels like a choice and not a dice roll
Clearer or more predictable handling of tanky/unparryable enemies in large mixed-enemy rooms
unique_things: Torch and brazier light management that changes both visibility and damage, rather than being just cosmetic lighting
Corruption meter that builds from room transitions and blood trades, spawning rule-changing curses instead of only giving buffs
Souls-like, turn-taking combat rhythm (strike then defend) in an isometric roguelite instead of Hades-style fast aggression
Parry-centred weakening/stun mechanic tied to blessings, with the sense of a slower, more deliberate run
Temple-by-temple structure with tiered boss sections and a distinctive Mesoamerican-inspired setting
Crossover content such as the Dead Cells weapon pack (April 2021)
tedious_or_disliked: Re-clearing the first section of each temple to reach deeper boss tiers, then repeating the whole structure for the final temple and hard mode
Grinding crystal skulls for weapons, blessings, rerolls and better starting gear, with some players saying normal difficulty feels gated by those hours
Rooms packed with five or more enemies, many tanky or unparryable, which slow the pace and undermine the parry mechanic
Teleporting/invulnerable enemies and screen-filling attacks in later temples that feel more like waiting than skill
Elite health-sponge enemies and high gold costs in the final temple
divisive_points: Whether it is a good roguelike or just a good action game: some say slow, methodical combat suits a run-based loop, others say it is a poor fit because runs are slow and repetitive
Difficulty and curses: some love the skill ceiling and risk-reward tension, others find late difficulty and RNG curses cheap
Progression pace: fans like slow unlocks that preserve weapon preferences, critics of it call the grind a chore
Hades comparison: praised as better combat and fairer, but clearly behind on story, art style and character
community.reception_notes: Metacritic PC critic score is 78 from 20 critic reviews (user score 6.9 from 112 ratings), verified on the Metacritic page. OpenCritic shows a Top Critic Average of 81 from 50 reviews with 86% recommending (Strong tier). IGN called it a standout roguelite; Nintendo Life compared the combat favorably to Hades; Game Informer felt it went stale after several runs. Launched from Early Access (March 2020, initially only the Jaguar section) to full release on 23 Feb 2021 on Windows, Switch, PS4 and Xbox One (no Mac/Linux). Steam price $19.99, SteamSpy owners estimate 500K-1M, about 84 concurrent players at time of data, and recent Steam reviews are still being posted, so it has an active if small audience. No major controversies found.
